questions.text: Quick Revision - Reflection of Light and Spherical Mirrors

definitionBean.title: Reflection of Light and Spherical Mirrors
definitionBean.definition: The bouncing back of light into the same medium after striking a shining surface is called 'reflection'; and mirrors with curved surfaces (concave and convex mirrors) converge or diverge light.
definitionBean.explanation: There are two laws of reflection: (1) The angle of incidence is always equal to the angle of reflection ($\angle i = \angle r$), (2) The incident ray, normal, and reflected ray all lie in the same plane.
importantPoints: Concave Mirror: Converging mirror (forms both real and virtual images)
Convex Mirror: Diverging mirror (always forms virtual, erect, and diminished images)

questions.text: Quick Revision - Refraction of Light and Lenses

definitionBean.title: Refraction of Light and Lenses
definitionBean.definition: The deviation (bending) of a light ray from its path when it passes from one transparent medium into another is called 'refraction'; and a medium bounded by transparent curved surfaces is called a 'lens'.
definitionBean.explanation: Refraction is based on Snell's law. A convex lens converges light while a concave lens diverges it. The unit of power of a lens is the dioptre (D).
importantPoints: Laws of refraction: Snell's law ($\frac{\sin i}{\sin r} = \text{constant}$)
Convex Lens: Converging lens (forms real and magnified/diminished images)
Concave Lens: Diverging lens (forms virtual and diminished images)

questions.text: Subject: Reflection of Light and Mirrors

parts.statement: Write the laws of reflection of light. State any two differences between a concave and a convex mirror.
parts.correct_answer: Laws of reflection are $\angle i = \angle r$ and coplanar; concave forms real and convex forms virtual images.
parts.explanation: Laws of reflection: 1. The angle of incidence and the angle of reflection are always equal ($\angle i = \angle r$). 2. The incident ray, reflected ray, and normal all lie in the same plane. The reflecting surface of a concave mirror curves inwards and it forms real images, whereas a convex mirror curves outwards and always forms virtual and smaller images.

parts.statement: Why is a convex mirror used as a rear-view mirror in vehicles? Explain the reason.
parts.correct_answer: A convex mirror has a wide field of view and forms erect and diminished images.
parts.explanation: A convex mirror has a very wide field of view because it curves outwards. It always forms an erect and diminished image of an object, giving the driver a clear view of a much larger area behind the vehicle.

questions.text: Subject: Refraction of Light and Lenses

parts.statement: Write the laws of refraction of light. What is Snell's law?
parts.correct_answer: Laws of refraction and $\frac{\sin i}{\sin r} = \text{constant}$ (Snell's law).
parts.explanation: Laws of refraction: 1. The incident ray, refracted ray, and normal all lie in the same plane. 2. For a given color of light and a given pair of media, the ratio of the sine of the angle of incidence ($\sin i$) to the sine of the angle of refraction ($\sin r$) is a constant, known as 'Snell's law' ($\frac{\sin i}{\sin r} = \text{constant}$).

parts.statement: What is meant by the power of a lens? Write its unit.
parts.correct_answer: Reciprocal of focal length is lens power, its unit is dioptre (D).
parts.explanation: The degree of convergence or divergence of light rays achieved by a lens is termed its power. It is equal to the reciprocal of focal length ($P = \frac{1}{f}$). Its SI unit is the 'dioptre' (Dioptre, D).
